calls.head: This one’s going to leave marks
calls.body: The Panthers and the Sharks are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 126.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Florida 142 (1st), San Jose 111 (7th)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 185, against their usual 126 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).
calls.beyond: Florida’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 239, against their usual 142 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games.

calls.head: Bring a pillow
calls.body: Florida plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does San Jose. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 79.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Florida 24th (79.9), San Jose 29th (79.4)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 75.5 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 79.4 and a league average of 81.5.

calls.head: The Panthers’ power play outclasses the Sharks’
calls.body: The Panthers are near the top of the league for the power play, at the lethal end; the Sharks are one of the league’s worst, at the harmless end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Panthers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Sharks’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Florida had 13.0 per 60 and San Jose 17.2 per 60. Coming in, Florida was at 7.8 per 60 and San Jose at 7.0 per 60.

SJS.head: We had this close to even (44% for San Jose), and San Jose came through.

FLA.head: We had this close to even (56% for Florida), and it went San Jose’s way.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 3.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 250 games.

surprises.head: San Jose’s power play came alive
surprises.body: San Jose’s power play created 17.2 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.0 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.
surprises.flipped: The Panthers’ power play outclasses the Sharks’

surprises.head: San Jose won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Florida wins 73. San Jose won anyway.

story.head: Askarov steals one
paras: Mason Marchment opened the scoring late in the first. Will Smith added two goals. Luca Cagnoni won it in overtime.
The Panthers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Panthers win about seven in ten. Yaroslav Askarov made the difference in net, stopping 23 of 26.

items.text: Two of the preview’s three calls held.
